subject: Slotted pricing tiers and ledger delivery automation
messages:
From: Sarah Alvarez <sarah@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing + export for monthly token commit

Hi Marissa,

We're evaluating a 12-month commit for Redwood hosted API and I wanted to check two things before we lock numbers:

1) Discount structure for "slotted" volume commits — our procurement model prefers a baseline commit and tiered pricing for increments (e.g., first X tokens at A, next slab at B). Do you have an example breakdown or a recommended slab configuration for a 750M/month baseline?

2) Billing transparency — we need an automated daily usage export (secure S3 preferred) that includes request-level token counts, model, route, and a request_id to reconcile against our own logs. Can Redwood provide both raw request-level CSV and a daily aggregated ledger that matches invoice line items (committed, overage by slab, credits)?

I've attached our internal forecast to give you scale. Also note procurement will require sample invoices and a quick notes on proration rules (mid-month starts, credits).

Can you share a proposed slab layout and confirm the export options? If helpful, happy to set up a 30-min sync.

Thanks,
Sarah Alvarez
Head of Procurement
Nimbus Health
Attachment: Nimbus-forecast.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Alvarez <sarah@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing + export for monthly token commit

Hi Sarah — great to hear from you and thanks for the forecast.

Short answers up front: yes — we support slabbed (slotted) commit tiers, and we can automate daily exports to S3 (or push to a BigQuery dataset / secure SFTP). We also produce invoice line items that map to the slabs used for that billing period.

Suggested slab for 750M/month (example, negotiable):
- 0 - 250M tokens: $0.00135/token (baseline)
- 250M - 750M tokens: $0.00105/token
- 750M - 2B tokens: $0.00090/token

With a 750M baseline commit we typically offer a blended committed price across the committed buckets and then apply overage rates per slab. If you prefer a stepped discount (where each slab is priced independently) we can show both numbers.

Export options:
- Raw request-level CSV (daily file): columns include date, request_id, route, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, user_id (if provided), and price_applied.
- Daily aggregated ledger (CSV): date, invoice_line_item_id, slab_bucket, total_tokens_in_bucket, billed_amount.

Invoice mapping and proration notes:
- Mid-month contract starts are prorated based on calendar days; we bill the prorated committed bucket and track remainder in month.
- Credits are issued as a line item and can be applied to the next invoice or as an immediate invoice adjustment for enterprise customers.

I've attached a short proposal PDF with the slab examples and delivery options. Can we grab 30 minutes tomorrow to confirm which slab model Nimbus prefers and the export destination?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: slotted-pricing-proposal.pdf

Hi all — quick technical confirmation and sample fields.

Delivery options we support (pick one or multiple):
- Daily S3 push (server-side encrypted, customer bucket or cross-account write)
- Daily BigQuery load (managed dataset in customer's project)
- Secure SFTP drop (enterprise only)

Sample raw request-level CSV fields (we can include additional optional fields):
- date (ISO)
- request_id (stable UUID per request; preserved across retries where retry is the same logical call; separate request_id for redirects)
- model (string)
- route (route name / endpoint)
- prompt_tokens (int)
- completion_tokens (int)
- total_tokens (int)
- user_id (if supplied by customer)
- price_per_token_applied (decimal)
- charged_amount (decimal)
- invoice_line_item_id (string)
- committed_bucket (e.g., "0-250M", "250M-750M")

Invoice mapping and slab handling (how charges appear):
- We calculate consumption per slab across billing period. Invoice includes separate line items for each slab with token totals and billed amount.
- Overage is computed against the slab unit price where consumption exceeded committed buckets.
- Proration: for mid-month starts, the committed bucket is prorated by days in the period; any unused proration is applied as a credit on the first full invoice.

Retention / audit: we retain request metadata and audit logs for 180 days by default for enterprise customers; we can extend retention to 365 days on contract. We can export full audit logs on request as a time-bound export (S3).

Attached is a small synthetic CSV example and a one-page invoice template that shows committed slab lines, overage lines, and credit/proration lines. Happy to walk through via the call — propose Tuesday 10/21 at 11am PT.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: billing-export-sample.csv
